 388 │ Custom Callbacks
 389 │ ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
 390 │ 
 391 │ You can also define your own callbacks. The callback should accept one
 392 │ parameter called ``retry_state`` that contains all information about current
 393 │ retry invocation.
 394 │ 
 395 │ For example, you can call a custom callback function after all retries failed,
 396 │ without raising an exception (or you can re-raise or do anything really)
 397 │ 
 398 │ .. testcode::
 399 │ 
 400 │     def return_last_value(retry_state):
 401 │         """return the result of the last call attempt"""
 402 │         return retry_state.outcome.result()
 403 │ 
 404 │     def is_false(value):
 405 │         """Return True if value is False"""
 406 │         return value is False
 407 │ 
 408 │     # will return False after trying 3 times to get a different result
 409 │     @retry(stop=stop_after_attempt(3),
 410 │            retry_error_callback=return_last_value,
 411 │            retry=retry_if_result(is_false))
 412 │     def eventually_return_false():
 413 │         return False
 414 │ 
 415 │ RetryCallState
 416 │ ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
 417 │ 
 418 │ ``retry_state`` argument is an object of :class:`~tenacity.RetryCallState` class.
 419 │ Its most useful attributes are:
 420 │ 
 421 │ * ``attempt_number`` — number of the current attempt (starts at 1)
 422 │ * ``outcome`` — a :class:`concurrent.futures.Future` holding the last result or exception
 423 │ * ``seconds_since_start`` — total elapsed seconds from the first attempt to the last outcome (``None`` if no outcome yet)
 424 │ * ``idle_for`` — cumulative seconds spent sleeping between attempts
 425 │ * ``start_time`` — :func:`time.monotonic` timestamp of the first attempt
 426 │ 
 427 │ For example, to log the total elapsed time after all retries:
 428 │ 
 429 │ .. testcode::
 430 │ 
 431 │     import logging
 432 │ 
 433 │     logging.basicConfig(stream=sys.stderr, level=logging.DEBUG)
 434 │ 
 435 │     logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
 436 │ 
 437 │     def log_elapsed(retry_state):
 438 │         logger.info('Finished after %.3fs', retry_state.seconds_since_start)
 439 │ 
 440 │     @retry(stop=stop_after_attempt(3), after=log_elapsed)
 441 │     def raise_my_exception():
 442 │         raise MyException("Fail")
 443 │ 
 444 │     try:
 445 │         raise_my_exception()
 446 │     except RetryError:
 447 │         pass
 448 │ 
 449 │ Other Custom Callbacks
 450 │ ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
 451 │ 
 452 │ It's also possible to define custom callbacks for other keyword arguments.
 453 │ 
 454 │ .. function:: my_stop(retry_state)
 455 │ 
 456 │    :param RetryCallState retry_state: info about current retry invocation
 457 │    :return: whether or not retrying should stop
 458 │    :rtype: bool
 459 │ 
 460 │ .. function:: my_wait(retry_state)
 461 │ 
 462 │    :param RetryCallState retry_state: info about current retry invocation
 463 │    :return: number of seconds to wait before next retry
 464 │    :rtype: float
 465 │ 
 466 │ .. function:: my_retry(retry_state)
 467 │ 
 468 │    :param RetryCallState retry_state: info about current retry invocation
 469 │    :return: whether or not retrying should continue
 470 │    :rtype: bool
 471 │ 
 472 │ .. function:: my_before(retry_state)
 473 │ 
 474 │    :param RetryCallState retry_state: info about current retry invocation
 475 │ 
 476 │ .. function:: my_after(retry_state)
 477 │ 
 478 │    :param RetryCallState retry_state: info about current retry invocation
 479 │ 
 480 │ .. function:: my_before_sleep(retry_state)
 481 │ 
 482 │    :param RetryCallState retry_state: info about current retry invocation
 483 │ 
 484 │ Here's an example with a custom ``before_sleep`` function:
 485 │ 
 486 │ .. testcode::
 487 │ 
 488 │     import logging
 489 │ 
 490 │     logging.basicConfig(stream=sys.stderr, level=logging.DEBUG)
 491 │ 
 492 │     logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
 493 │ 
 494 │     def my_before_sleep(retry_state):
 495 │         if retry_state.attempt_number < 1:
 496 │             loglevel = logging.INFO
 497 │         else:
 498 │             loglevel = logging.WARNING
 499 │         logger.log(
 500 │             loglevel, 'Retrying %s: attempt %s ended with: %s',
 501 │             retry_state.fn, retry_state.attempt_number, retry_state.outcome)
 502 │ 
 503 │     @retry(stop=stop_after_attempt(3), before_sleep=my_before_sleep)
 504 │     def raise_my_exception():
 505 │         raise MyException("Fail")
 506 │ 
 507 │     try:
 508 │         raise_my_exception()
 509 │     except RetryError:
 510 │         pass
 511 │

 513 │ Common Patterns
 514 │ ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
 515 │ 
 516 │ **Running setup code between retries** (e.g. reconnecting):
 517 │ 
 518 │ .. testcode::
 519 │ 
 520 │     def reconnect(retry_state):
 521 │         print("Reconnecting before next attempt...")
 522 │ 
 523 │     @retry(stop=stop_after_attempt(3), before_sleep=reconnect)
 524 │     def send_data():
 525 │         raise MyException("connection lost")
 526 │ 
 527 │     try:
 528 │         send_data()
 529 │     except RetryError:
 530 │         pass

 533 │    :hide:
 534 │ 
 535 │    ...
 536 │ 
 537 │ The ``before_sleep`` callback runs after a failed attempt and before sleeping,
 538 │ making it ideal for re-establishing connections, refreshing tokens, or any
 539 │ other setup that needs to happen before the next attempt.
 540 │ 
 541 │ **Accessing the attempt number inside the function** using the iterator API:
 542 │ 
 543 │ .. testcode::
 544 │ 
 545 │     from tenacity import Retrying
 546 │ 
 547 │     for attempt in Retrying(stop=stop_after_attempt(3)):
 548 │         with attempt:
 549 │             print(f"Attempt {attempt.retry_state.attempt_number}")
 550 │             if attempt.retry_state.attempt_number < 3:
 551 │                 raise MyException("not yet")

 559 │ Changing Arguments at Run Time
 560 │ ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
 561 │ 
 562 │ You can change the arguments of a retry decorator as needed when calling it by
 563 │ using the `retry_with` function attached to the wrapped function:
 564 │ 
 565 │ .. testcode::
 566 │ 
 567 │     @retry(stop=stop_after_attempt(3))
 568 │     def raise_my_exception():
 569 │         raise MyException("Fail")
 570 │ 
 571 │     try:
 572 │         raise_my_exception.retry_with(stop=stop_after_attempt(4))()
 573 │     except Exception:
 574 │         pass
 575 │ 
 576 │     print(raise_my_exception.statistics)
 577 │

 579 │    :hide:
 580 │ 
 581 │    ...
 582 │ 
 583 │ If you want to use variables to set up the retry parameters, you don't have
 584 │ to use the `retry` decorator - you can instead use `Retrying` directly:
 585 │ 
 586 │ .. testcode::
 587 │ 
 588 │     def never_good_enough(arg1):
 589 │         raise Exception('Invalid argument: {}'.format(arg1))
 590 │ 
 591 │     def try_never_good_enough(max_attempts=3):
 592 │         retryer = Retrying(stop=stop_after_attempt(max_attempts), reraise=True)
 593 │         retryer(never_good_enough, 'I really do try')
 594 │ 
 595 │ You may also want to change the behaviour of a decorated function temporarily,
 596 │ like in tests to avoid unnecessary wait times. You can modify/patch the `retry`
 597 │ attribute attached to the function. Bear in mind this is a write-only attribute,
 598 │ statistics should be read from the function `statistics` attribute.
 599 │ 
 600 │ .. testcode::
 601 │ 
 602 │     @retry(stop=stop_after_attempt(3), wait=wait_fixed(3))
 603 │     def raise_my_exception():
 604 │         raise MyException("Fail")
 605 │ 
 606 │     from unittest import mock
 607 │ 
 608 │     with mock.patch.object(raise_my_exception.retry, "wait", wait_fixed(0)):
 609 │         try:
 610 │             raise_my_exception()
 611 │         except Exception:
 612 │             pass
 613 │ 
 614 │     print(raise_my_exception.statistics)

 621 │ Retrying code block
 622 │ ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
 623 │ 
 624 │ Tenacity allows you to retry a code block without the need to wraps it in an
 625 │ isolated function. This makes it easy to isolate failing block while sharing
 626 │ context. The trick is to combine a for loop and a context manager.
 627 │ 
 628 │ .. testcode::
 629 │ 
 630 │    from tenacity import Retrying, RetryError, stop_after_attempt
 631 │ 
 632 │    try:
 633 │        for attempt in Retrying(stop=stop_after_attempt(3)):
 634 │            with attempt:
 635 │                raise Exception('My code is failing!')
 636 │    except RetryError:
 637 │        pass
 638 │ 
 639 │ You can configure every details of retry policy by configuring the Retrying
 640 │ object.
 641 │ 
 642 │ With async code you can use AsyncRetrying.
 643 │ 
 644 │ .. testcode::
 645 │ 
 646 │    from tenacity import AsyncRetrying, RetryError, stop_after_attempt
 647 │ 
 648 │    async def function():
 649 │       try:
 650 │           async for attempt in AsyncRetrying(stop=stop_after_attempt(3)):
 651 │               with attempt:
 652 │                   raise Exception('My code is failing!')
 653 │       except RetryError:
 654 │           pass
 655 │ 
 656 │ In both cases, you may want to set the result to the attempt so it's available
 657 │ in retry strategies like ``retry_if_result``. This can be done accessing the
 658 │ ``retry_state`` property:
 659 │ 
 660 │ .. testcode::
 661 │ 
 662 │     from tenacity import AsyncRetrying, retry_if_result
 663 │ 
 664 │     async def function():
 665 │        async for attempt in AsyncRetrying(retry=retry_if_result(lambda x: x < 3)):
 666 │            with attempt:
 667 │                result = 1  # Some complex calculation, function call, etc.
 668 │            if not attempt.retry_state.outcome.failed:
 669 │                attempt.retry_state.set_result(result)
 670 │        return result
 671 │
